appraisal_events.evidence: Norpois delivers a long, self-important tirade insisting the Constantinople post go to 'un homme de haute valeur... qui aurait, si je puis dire, l'oreille de l'empereur,' his irritation traceable to the newspapers naming a young minister as favorite instead of him.
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator lets Norpois's own pompous, thinly veiled self-advocacy run on, exposing petty vanity and envy of a rival beneath his lofty diplomatic rhetoric.

status_effects.explanation: His grandiose speech is undercut by the evident personal vanity and envy driving it, locally diminishing him even as he speaks with apparent authority.
